column2: The Lord speaks on Mount Sinai; the location is explicit and preserved with the inherited name form.
The land which I give is repeated before its Sabbath rest. The repetition is retained as part of the divine gift framing.
Six years of field sowing and six years of vine pruning precede fruit gathering. The repeated duration remains.
Seventh-year rest belongs to the land and the Lord. Both sowing and pruning are prohibited.
Self-grown crops and grapes of consecration are not harvested. The Greek sanctification wording is preserved rather than replaced by a vine-care explanation.
Sabbath produce is the contextual food referent. Its beneficiaries include owner, male and female slaves, hired worker and attached lodger.
All produce also feeds livestock and wild animals. The animal beneficiaries are not omitted from the distribution.
Seven rests, seven times seven years and forty-nine years express the same count three ways. All remain.
Trumpet proclamation across the land is repeated, with the tenth of the seventh month identified as atonement day.
Fiftieth-year consecration and release lead to possession and homeland returns. Signal provisionally represents semasia alongside release.
column3: Does semasia require a more idiomatic festival designation while retaining its signal sense?

column2: The fiftieth year prohibits sowing and harvesting spontaneous or consecrated produce. The year-of-release formula is retained.
Holy status and eating directly from fields qualify the harvest restrictions. The food permission is explicit.
Each returns to possession at the release-year signal. No automatic modern ownership formula is substituted.
Selling and buying both prohibit oppressing the neighbour. The Greek person shifts are retained in the conditional framing.
Price is related to years after the signal and harvest years sold. The two parties' perspectives remain distinct.
More years increase the price; fewer decrease it. The reason is the number of harvests being transferred.
The non-oppression command is repeated and grounded in fear of God. Singular and plural divine-address objects remain ordinary your.
All statutes and judgments are to be done, kept and done again. Confident dwelling follows; the repeated doing is source-supported.
Land yield, eating to fullness and confident dwelling are linked promises. Fullness is not merely a generic sufficient-food paraphrase.
The anticipated question concerns food during the seventh year without sowing or gathering. It is kept as a direct question.
Blessing in the sixth year provides produce for three years. The feminine land referent behind its is implicit.
Sowing resumes in the eighth year while stored produce lasts until the ninth harvest. The repeated old wording is retained.
Permanent alienation is prohibited because the land belongs to the Lord. Israel's status as foreigners and lodgers before Him remains.
Redemption is to be provided throughout the possessed land. The general rule precedes the specific poverty cases.
An impoverished brother sells part of his holding; the nearest redeeming kinsman recovers it. The nearness emphasis is represented.
Absence of a redeeming kinsman and later sufficient means introduce self-redemption. The hand idiom remains provisional.
The Greek says sold himself despite the preceding property context. That reflexive is preserved rather than silently changed to sold it.
column3: Apparatus and syntax review should assess the reflexive in this property-redemption sequence.

column2: The source explicitly reads sixth year of release. This difficult reading is retained, with return at release afterward.
column3: Investigate the sixth-year phrase in apparatus and textual commentary; no emendation is credited here.

column2: A walled-city dwelling has a full-year redemption period. The repeated redemption wording is represented naturally as the period.
After the complete year, ownership is confirmed permanently across the buyer's generations; release does not apply.
Unwalled settlement houses count with agricultural land, remaining redeemable and released. The contrast with walled cities is explicit.
Levitical city houses are always redeemable by Levites. Their special status is not generalized to all city property.
The opening redemption construction is difficult; the sale of Levitical houses goes out at release because it is their possession within Israel.
column3: Who is the opening redeemer, and what precise transaction does the participial construction describe?

column2: The fields assigned to Levitical cities cannot be sold because they are an enduring possession. The fields differ from the houses.
An impoverished brother with weakened means is supported as foreigner and lodger, so he lives with the addressee.
column3: Does as a resident foreigner and lodger qualify his status or the standard of support to be given?

column2: Interest and increase are both forbidden; fear of God and the brother's continued life are linked. The source's I am the Lord remains.
Silver and food have separate interest/increase prohibitions. Both lending categories remain explicit.
The exodus leads to giving Canaan and being their God. Both purposes are retained.
The impoverished brother sold into service is not to serve as a household slave. The restriction is not expanded beyond its stated kin group.
Hired-worker or lodger status lasts until release. The two comparisons remain distinct from permanent enslavement.
Release includes his children and return to kin and ancestral holding. Return renders the movement verb idiomatically without implying flight from pursuit.
The Lord's ownership of the exodus people grounds their exemption from slave sale. The singular final subject is represented impersonally.
Wearing him down through toil is prohibited, with fear of God as the parallel command. The labour-specific wording remains.
The text permits acquiring male and female slaves from surrounding nations. The enslaved status is stated plainly without euphemistic employment terminology.
Acquisition also includes lodgers' descendants and relatives in the land. Their possession status is explicit.
Slaves may be transmitted to children and held permanently; the prohibition of oppressive toil is specifically directed to Israelite brethren.
A prosperous foreigner/lodger may acquire an impoverished brother. Foreigner by birth retains the final Greek qualification provisionally.
column3: How does ek genetes proselyto relate to the two preceding purchaser descriptions?

column2: Sale does not remove redemption; a brother can redeem him. Right of redemption expresses the legal availability.
Uncle, cousin, other tribal flesh-kin and self-redemption are successive possibilities. The hand-based means idiom remains.
Years from sale to release determine the price in relation to hired-worker pay. Both parties participate in calculation.
Many remaining years require proportionate repayment from sale money. Proportionality, not a fixed price, governs.
Few remaining years require a correspondingly calculated redemption. The alternative is not collapsed into the preceding larger amount.
Hired-worker treatment is year by year. The Greek command is you shall not wear him down, not he shall not; the person shift is retained.
If earlier redemption does not occur, release still includes the person and his children in the release year.
Israel's servitude to the Lord is expressed with two servant nouns and grounded in the exodus. The inherited distinction remains provisional, without softening the ownership metaphor.
Handmade images, carvings, pillar and conspicuous stone are distinct prohibited objects for worship. Conspicuous stone remains a provisional skopos interpretation.
column3: Does lithos skopos denote a conspicuous marker, figured stone or another cultic object?

column2: Sabbath keeping and reverence for holy things repeat the established paired commands. The plural holy expression remains.
Walking, keeping and doing form the condition for the promises that follow. None is reduced to mental assent alone.
Seasonal rain brings land produce and tree fruit. The two agricultural subjects and outputs remain distinct.
Threshing reaches vintage, and vintage reaches sowing, expressing abundant continuity. Satisfaction and secure dwelling follow.
The Greek begins with no war through the land, then peace, safe sleep and removal of harmful animals. The order is preserved.
Enemies fall in slaughter after pursuit. The source's phonos is not automatically replaced by sword, which occurs next.
Five pursue a hundred and a hundred pursue myriads, plural. Tens of thousands preserves that plural rather than fixing one ten-thousand group.
Divine regard, increase, multiplication and covenant establishment are four actions. The growth verbs remain distinct.
Old stores are repeated with intensification, then removed before new produce. The repetitive abundance image is retained.
The selected Greek says covenant among you, not tabernacle. The divine soul's refusal to abhor is preserved.
Walking among the people and the reciprocal God/people relationship remain. No embodiment explanation is inserted into the metaphor.
Slavery, broken yoke-bond and boldness describe liberation. Boldness reflects parrhesia rather than substituting upright posture.
Failure to obey and failure to do these ordinances introduce the contrary condition. Both negatives remain.
Disobedience and inner indignation lead to not doing commandments and dissolving covenant. The two result/purpose clauses remain.
Distress, skin affliction and jaundice-like illness, wasting eyes/life and enemy-eaten seed remain. The inherited medical labels are provisional ancient-term renderings.
column3: Confirm psora, ikteros and sphakelizo in context without equating them with precise modern diagnoses.

column2: The Lord sets His face against them; enemies pursue, yet panic also causes flight without pursuit. Both situations are retained.
Continued disobedience brings added sevenfold discipline. Seven times more renders the added-discipline construction rather than a calculated total of punishments.
Arrogance of pride is broken; iron heaven and bronze-like earth remain two distinct images.
Strength becomes futile, land fails to yield seed and trees fail to yield fruit. Seed is the selected noun here.
Crooked walking and unwillingness to obey lead to seven blows according to sins. The source says seven blows, not seven times in this clause.
Wild animals devour people, consume livestock and reduce their number, leaving roads desolate. The destructive agency is retained.
Failure to be disciplined introduces continued crooked conduct toward God. The passive learning/discipline relation remains.
Divine contrary anger answers crooked walking; I too is repeated. The reciprocal phrasing is not softened away.
A covenant-avenging sword, flight to cities, death and surrender to enemies are successive threats. Death is not silently replaced with a specific plague.
Ten women share one oven and ration bread by weight. The emphatic lack of satisfaction remains after eating.
The disobedience condition repeats after these further events. The cumulative structure is preserved.
I Myself and I emphasize divine response; sevenfold discipline is according to sins. Both emphatic pronouns are represented.
Sons' and daughters' flesh are both named, with eating repeated. The severe famine image is translated without added detail.
Pillars, wooden handmade images and limbs upon idol limbs follow this Greek wording. The divine soul's indignation remains.
column3: Does kola here mean limbs, corpses or ruined bodies in the two contrasting applications?

column2: Cities and holy places are desolated, and the sacrificial scent is refused. The emphatic negative is represented.
The Lord explicitly desolates the land; resident enemies marvel. Their reaction is not changed into approval.
Scattering among nations and the advancing sword leave land and cities desolate. The sword is the grammatical consuming agent.
The land welcomes its Sabbaths during exile and desolation. The repeated personification is retained.
Desolation supplies rests previously denied while Israel inhabited the land. The repeated Sabbath vocabulary remains visible.
A wind-borne leaf's sound drives fearful flight and falling without pursuit. The source says war in the comparison, not necessarily sword.
Brother disregards brother in the selected Greek. Stumbling over one another is not substituted from a different base.
Perishing among nations and the enemy land's devouring are both stated. The land's metaphorical agency remains.
The survivors suffer because of your sins, then waste in their enemies' land. The source's second-to-third-person change is retained.
Confession includes their own and their fathers' sins, with transgression, disregard and crooked walking as explanations.
Past divine contrary conduct shifts to future destruction, then shame and accepting sins. The difficult sequence is retained rather than harmonized to an expected repentance formula.
column3: Does accepting sins signify accepting their consequences? Confirm the lexical relation without inserting penalty silently.

column2: Jacob, Isaac and Abraham appear in that order, with covenant and remembering repeated, followed by remembrance of the land.
The abandoned land receives Sabbaths, while the people receive/accept their lawless deeds. The parallel verb and their earlier disregard remain.
column3: Should accepting lawless deeds be rendered accepting responsibility or consequences, and what supports that metonymy?

column2: The Greek uses past negative verbs for disregard and indignation even amid exile. Their purpose/result limit is total consumption and covenant dissolution.
The earlier covenant is remembered with exodus from a house of slavery before the nations. The additional house-of-slavery clause remains.
Judgments, ordinances and law were given between the Lord and Israel on Sinai through Moses. All three categories and mediation remain.
The Lord speaks to Moses, introducing valuation and dedication rules after the covenant conclusion.
Vowing a vow and valuation of one's person are connected. Soul is the inherited personal idiom, not a claim about monetary valuation of an immaterial soul.
column3: Would person make the legal valuation clearer while preserving psyche's sense here?

column2: Male age twenty to sixty is valued at fifty silver didrachmas by sacred weight. Neither age endpoints nor denomination is silently modernized.
The female assessment is thirty didrachmas within the preceding age band. The inherited elliptical connection is retained.
Ages five to twenty have twenty didrachmas for male and ten for female. Both amounts and the age interval agree with the source.
One month to five years has five silver didrachmas for male and three for female. The lower endpoint is one month, not one year.
Sixty and upward has fifteen for male and ten for female. The inclusive upward qualification remains.
Poverty permits priestly valuation according to means. The hand-strength idiom is retained in the literary draft, with a more natural spoken alternative recorded.
An eligible sacrificial animal given to the Lord becomes holy. The rule concerns the given animal, not every animal its owner possesses.
Both good-for-bad and bad-for-good exchanges are forbidden; attempted substitution makes both animals holy. The doubled exchange form supports does exchange.
An unclean animal unsuitable for offering is set before the priest for valuation. No sacrifice of it is prescribed.
The priest assesses between good and bad, and his assessment stands. The quality scale is retained provisionally.
column3: Would according to its quality better communicate the idiom without removing its two poles?

column2: Redemption requires the assessed amount plus one fifth. The emphatic redemption construction supports does redeem.
A consecrated house is assessed on the same good/bad scale. The priest's valuation remains binding.
The consecrator may recover the house with an added fifth of assessed silver. Possession then returns to him.
Inherited field valuation depends on seed capacity, fifty silver didrachmas per kor of barley. No land-area conversion is invented.
Consecration from the release year uses the full standing valuation. The temporal preposition remains from.
Later consecration requires calculation by remaining years and a deduction. The reduction is not treated as an added surcharge.
Field redemption by its consecrator adds one fifth to the assessment. The field then belongs to him again.
Failure to redeem followed by sale to another removes further redemption. The repeated field object remains for clarity.
column3: Who is the understood seller in the second clause within this legal sequence?

column2: The release having passed, the field is holy like set-apart land and becomes priestly possession. The perfect temporal expression is retained.
A purchased field is explicitly distinguished from inherited possession. The different return rule follows in verse 24.
The Greek says valuation from the release year, followed by same-day payment. The preposition is retained despite the difficult calculation context.
column3: How does ek tou eniautou relate to total valuation here, compared with the until formulation at verse 18?

column2: At release the purchased field returns to the original holder from whom it was acquired. The inherited holding relationship remains explicit.
All assessments use sacred weights, and the source assigns twenty obols to the didrachma. No classical coin conversion replaces this stated equivalence.
Firstborn livestock already belongs to the Lord and cannot be newly consecrated. Calf and sheep remain the inherited examples.
column3: Does probaton here cover the wider flock category? No universal sheep-to-flock replacement has been made.

column2: An unclean quadruped is exchanged at valuation plus a fifth, or sold at valuation if not redeemed. Exchange and redemption remain distinct verbs.
Devoted persons, animals and land cannot be sold or redeemed and are most holy. The category is not equated automatically with an ordinary vow.
column3: Establish the precise scope of anathema dedication through contextual and specialist review before acceptance.

column2: The devoted human category is expressly nonredeemable and subject to the emphatic death formula. The severity is neither omitted nor expanded.
Land tithe includes seed and tree fruit and belongs to the Lord. Both produce categories and holiness remain.
Redeeming a tithe requires an additional fifth. Indeed is supported by the cognate redemption expression.
Cattle and flock animals pass under the counting staff; the tenth is holy. The counting image is retained without an invented sorting procedure.
Good-for-bad exchange is forbidden; attempted exchange sanctifies the substitute as well. The final no-redemption rule remains.
The book closes with the commandments given to Moses for Israel at Sinai. The recipient chain and location remain explicit.
